formula: y_n ~ Normal(mu + year_re[year_ind[n]] + region_re[region_ind[n]] + state_re[state_ind[n]] + GP_region[year_ind[n],region_ind[n]] + GP_state[year_ind[n],state_ind[n]], sigma_error); state scales vary by region; each GP family shares long+short squared-exponential kernels across levels; all 17 variances share a Dirichlet variance budget
documented_prior: mu ~ normal(.5, .5); tot_var ~ gamma(3, 3); prop_var ~ dirichlet(rep(2, 17)); length_GP_*_long ~ weibull(30, 8); length_GP_*_short ~ weibull(30, 3)
notes: rendered from Stan (hierarchical_gp); state presidential vote shares (StanCon 2017 Trangucci). Random intercepts for state, region (states nested in regions) and year, plus two Gaussian-process smooths over year (region and state level) that lme4 cannot express. y is a vote share (proportion) modelled Normal. RULE GAP: model combines hierarchical random intercepts with Gaussian processes; the brief excludes pure GP models, but this has genuine hierarchical terms, so kept with the GP noted. Code read #15: the state effect has one scale per region (state_re = sigma_state[state_region_ind] .* state_std, hierarchical_gp.stan:75), and the region-by-year and state-by-year GPs enter the mean (:105-109), each a sum of a long and a short squared-exponential kernel with hyperparameters shared across levels (brms gp(by =) would give each level its own); all 17 variances (year, region, 10 regional state scales, 4 GP magnitudes, residual) are 17 * prop_var * tot_var, tot_var ~ gamma(3, 3), prop_var ~ dirichlet(rep(2, 17)) (:60-71), a shared variance budget brms cannot state; one row per state-year (550 = 50 x 11), so the state GP is observation-level. Hand sample #12: the brms-like shorthand changed the source's covariance structure; the formula now writes the Stan mean. year_ind is also the GPs' time input, kept as a grouping factor only (a column is never both).
